newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND IN GROOVE AS BAYERN SUFFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND IN GROOVE AS BAYERN SUFFER.

text.p: German league leaders Borussia Dortmund look forward to a top-of-the-table clash at VfB Stuttgart on Saturday with a comforting thought -- rivals Bayern Munich are frustrated and fretting.

A 3-0 win over Hansa Rostock on Wednesday secured the reigning champions a three-point lead at the top while second-placed Bayern suffered their second defeat in four days at the hands of unfancied Armenia Bielefeld.
Bayern chairman Franz Beckenbauer was livid about his team's calamitous 5-2 reverse at Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday and Wednesday's 2-0 loss at promoted Bielefeld.

"Perhaps we are going to have to change our goals for the season. The way they are playing at the moment I'm afraid we may not qualify for the UEFA Cup," the former World Cup-winning coach and captain said.
"We are not aggressive enough. We're standing off our opponents. If I got that much space, I'd would still be able to play today."

Bayern's German international midfielder Thomas Strunz added: "Things are looking different in Dortmund. Their recent victory in the European Cup has given them an extra boost. They seem to be in a groove."

Third-placed Stuttgart managed a 1-1 draw at European Cup quarter-finalists Dortmund in the first half of the season and have really hit form in the last week, thumping five goals past Cologne on Tuesday and four past Hamburg last weekend.
They are now just two points behind Bayern but ahead of Leverkusen only on goal difference and Saturday's game is one of the most fascinating of the season.
"I always knew we would get back to our best," Stuttgart's German international striker Fredi Bobic said. "Our run of form at the start of the season showed what potential we have in the team."
Stuttgart and fourth-placed Bayer Leverkusen are just two points behind Bayern in a tight battle at the top.
Bayern, who had lost just once in 20 matches all season before the Leverkusen defeat, need to bounce back to form quickly before the traditional internal squabbling starts.
The Bavarians have an awkward home game against fifth-placed Schalke on Saturday.

"In both games we slept in the first half. Why? I don't know," Strunz said of the defeats. "It is possible that there will be the typical over-reaction in Munich. But it is in a situation like this that we need to show that we're a team."
Munich's conquerors, Leverkusen and Bielefeld, meet on Saturday.
